---
title: "Assignment 3: Do Two Sites Differ in Artifact Length? (Instructor Solution)"
format: html
---

Instructor solution. The grader runs this file once and uses it to confirm the
rubric's object names. Do not hand this file out. See `docs/conventions.md`.

```{r load-data}
artifacts <- read.csv("artifacts.csv")
two_sites <- subset(artifacts, site %in% c("River Terrace", "Cave Mouth"))
```

## Task 1: Test the difference in mean length

```{r run-test}
river <- two_sites$length_mm[two_sites$site == "River Terrace"]
cave <- two_sites$length_mm[two_sites$site == "Cave Mouth"]

ttest_result <- t.test(river, cave)   # Welch two-sample t-test
t_statistic <- unname(ttest_result$statistic)
p_value <- ttest_result$p.value
conf_int <- as.numeric(ttest_result$conf.int)
```

## Task 2: Effect size

```{r effect-size}
sd_pooled <- sqrt(((length(river) - 1) * var(river) + (length(cave) - 1) * var(cave)) /
                    (length(river) + length(cave) - 2))
cohens_d <- (mean(river) - mean(cave)) / sd_pooled
```

## Interpretation

River Terrace artifacts are about 6.5 mm longer than Cave Mouth artifacts on
average (42.1 mm against 35.6 mm). A Welch two-sample t-test gives t = 4.25 and
p < 0.001, with a 95% confidence interval for the difference of about 3.5 to
9.6 mm, so the difference is very unlikely to be due to chance alone. The effect
size is large (Cohen's d is about 1.0): the average River Terrace artifact is
roughly one standard deviation longer than the average Cave Mouth artifact.
